data.title: Pyogenic granuloma (lobular capillary haemangioma) — viva
data.summary: Vascular & ulcers · 9 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Pyogenic granuloma (lobular capillary haemangioma)** (Vascular & ulcers)_

**Q1. What is pyogenic granuloma (PG)?**
- Common acquired benign vascular tumour (lobular capillary haemangioma) of skin and mucosa; neither infective ('pyogenic') nor granulomatous — misnomer; children and young adults, pregnant women (granuloma gravidarum/epulis on gingiva)

**Q2. Triggers / associations.**
- Minor trauma (often), pregnancy and OCPs (hormonal), burns, ingrown toenails
- Drugs: systemic retinoids (isotretinoin, acitretin — periungual), EGFR inhibitors (cetuximab, gefitinib — periungual), BRAF/MEK inhibitors, capecitabine, antiretrovirals (indinavir), cyclosporine, taxanes
- Multiple/satellite PG after removal; within port-wine stains

**Q3. Describe the lesion.**
- Rapidly growing (weeks) solitary bright red, friable, sessile or pedunculated papule/nodule (5–10 mm), with glistening or eroded surface and a collarette of scale at its base
- Bleeds profusely with minor trauma; sites — fingers, lips, face, gingiva, scalp, nail folds

**Q4. Histopathology.**
- Exophytic polypoid lesion with lobules of proliferating capillaries separated by fibrous septa, a central feeding vessel, surface ulceration with inflammation, epidermal collarette at the base (inward-growing rete ridges)
- GLUT-1 negative (vs infantile haemangioma)

**Q5. Differential diagnosis.**
- Amelanotic melanoma (most important — any atypical/recurrent PG should be biopsied and sent for histology), SCC/keratoacanthoma, Kaposi sarcoma, bacillary angiomatosis (HIV — Bartonella), glomus tumour, cherry angioma, infantile haemangioma, Spitz naevus, metastasis, granulation tissue (ingrown nail), angiosarcoma, eccrine poroma

**Q6. Treatment.**
- Shave excision with curettage and cautery of the base (electrodesiccation) — lowest recurrence when the feeding vessel is cauterised; send tissue for histopathology
- Surgical excision with closure (recurrence lowest), cryotherapy, laser (pulsed-dye, CO2, Nd:YAG), silver nitrate cautery for small lesions
- Topical timolol 0.5% (children, periungual), imiquimod, sodium tetradecyl sulphate sclerotherapy
- Pregnancy-related: may regress after delivery; drug-induced: dose reduction, topical timolol

**Q7. Write short notes on glomus tumour (PYQ).**
- Benign tumour of the glomus body (modified smooth muscle cells regulating thermoregulatory arteriovenous shunts — Sucquet–Hoyer canal)
- Solitary: subungual blue-red spot with severe paroxysmal pain, cold sensitivity and point tenderness — Love's pin test, Hildreth's test (pain abolished by tourniquet), cold sensitivity test; X-ray may show bony erosion; MRI
- Multiple glomuvenous malformations (glomangiomas) — autosomal dominant (glomulin), less painful, children
- Treatment: surgical excision

**Q8. What is granuloma gravidarum?**
- PG on the gingiva in pregnancy (epulis gravidarum) — hormones (progesterone/oestrogen) and gingivitis; often regresses after delivery; excise if bleeding or interfering with eating

**Q9. What is bacillary angiomatosis and why differentiate?**
- Bartonella henselae/quintana infection in HIV (CD4 <100) — multiple PG-like red papules/nodules, systemic (liver — peliosis, bone); Warthin–Starry stain shows bacilli; treated with erythromycin/doxycycline for months — not with excision alone

## Quick spotter facts
- Rapidly growing bleeding red papule with collarette — pyogenic granuloma
- Always send for histology — exclude amelanotic melanoma
- Subungual painful blue spot + cold sensitivity — glomus tumour

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Vascular tumours). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
